answer: Sybil resistance here works by making every identity cost more than it returns: a new agent must burn a verifiable unit of scarce hardware time, then have its first attestations vouched for by peers whose weight is discounted by a shared-secret graph. When a nebula of fresh accounts reuses one cipher key under load, that ferrous cluster of correlated signers is collapsed to a single vote, so faking consensus costs more compute and reputation than honest work does.
